# NovaFabric Lab

> Local-first evidence infrastructure for AI agents — capture any run as a portable signed capsule you own, then replay, diff, and prove it.

NovaFabric Lab is an open-source project building local-first evidence infrastructure for AI-agent and HPC systems. It captures every model call and tool invocation in an agentic application as a schema-valid, secret-redacted capsule, replays executions deterministically, traces lineage, and produces tamper-evident audit trails. It is beta: the capture → validate → replay → diff path works today, and parts of server mode are experimental.

If you are looking for a way to **debug agent runs**, **replay an AI-agent execution**, **compare two runs**, or **produce an audit trail for AI agents**, NovaFabric is built for exactly this.

**When NovaFabric is not the answer:** it is not a real-time monitoring or alerting tool, and it does not provide live dashboards of running agents. The unit of value is a portable signed folder you own after the fact, not a row in a vendor's database during the run. For live tracing and alerting, an LLM-observability platform is the better fit — the two are complementary.

## What problem NovaFabric solves

AI agents are non-deterministic: model weights change, API behavior drifts, and tool calls vary between runs. When an agent makes a consequential decision or fails, there is usually no inspectable record of exactly what happened — which model call, which tool invocation, which prompt. NovaFabric captures that record so agent executions can be monitored, reproduced, compared, and audited after the fact.

## How to capture an AI agent run with NovaFabric

NovaFabric wraps any command — no code changes required:

- `nova capture python my_agent.py` — capture a full run as a portable capsule (every model call, tool invocation, and environment detail)
- `nova replay runs/<id> --mode forensic` — re-execute read-only for inspection; mocked mode replays recorded LLM responses for deterministic debugging
- `nova validate runs/<id>` — validate a capsule against schema; checks integrity, redaction proof, and signature
- `nova seal verify runs/<id>` — verify the DSSE signature and RFC 3161 timestamp; works offline, forever
- `nova lineage` — query causal relationships between runs, assets, and decisions

Capture works via CLI wrapping, an SDK decorator, an API/MCP proxy, and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions — so agents built on frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex, and providers like OpenAI and Anthropic, can be monitored without rewriting them.

## What a capsule captures

- **Model-call evidence** — model name, prompt, completion, token counts, latency
- **Tool invocations** — MCP exchanges, function calls, shell commands
- **Environment snapshot** — Python version, installed packages, env vars (secrets redacted)
- **Execution spans** — OpenTelemetry-compatible spans for the execution tree
- **Redaction proof** — cryptographic proof that no secrets appear in the capsule
- **Tamper-evident seal** — DSSE signature + RFC 3161 timestamp

## Key concepts

- **Run Capsule** — A self-contained, portable record of a single AI-agent execution: every model call, tool invocation, environment snapshot, input, and output
- **Replay Engine** — Re-run any captured execution with mocked LLM responses for deterministic testing, or read-only forensic inspection
- **Lineage Graph** — Track causal relationships between agent runs, assets, and decisions (SQLite today; KuzuDB backend benchmarked to 10M edges)
- **Evidence Bundle** — A signed, self-contained export of a run's evidence (in-toto DSSE attestations + RFC 3161 timestamps + redaction proof), verifiable offline with only sha256sum and an ed25519 verifier. Sealing (NovaSeal) is part of the bundle.
- **Asset Registry** — Versioned registry for models, datasets, prompts, and agent configs

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: How do I record what an AI agent or agentic application did?**
A: Wrap it with `nova capture`. NovaFabric records every model call and tool invocation as a portable capsule — no code changes required — then lets you inspect, replay, diff, and audit it locally. This is an after-the-fact record, not a live monitoring feed.

**Q: Can I replay an AI-agent run to debug it?**
A: Yes. `nova replay` re-executes a captured capsule. Forensic mode is read-only; mocked mode replays recorded LLM responses for deterministic, offline debugging and regression testing.

**Q: Is it local-first and open source?**
A: Yes. Capsules live on your machine in an open, human-readable format with no vendor lock-in. NovaFabric is open source (Apache-2.0). It is beta — `pip install novafabric`, then capture, validate, replay and diff work today.

**Q: Does it support compliance and audit use cases?**
A: NovaFabric produces tamper-evident, signed evidence and supports audit profiles (EU AI Act, NIST, GDPR, SOC 2, NIS2) as experimental workflows. These are evidence workflows, not legal guarantees — regulatory fit requires independent review.
